subject: general
question: For an experiment with sample space S, the events Aᵢ, i = 1, 2, 3,.... are mutually exclusive and exhaustive if:

options.text: ⋃ᵢAᵢ = S and Aᵢ ∪ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j
⋃iAi = S and Aᵢ ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j
Ai ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j

solution:
The correct answer is **⋃iAi = S and Ai ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

In the context of an experiment with a sample space S, the events Ai, i = 1, 2, 3, ..., are formally defined as mutually exclusive and exhaustive if the following conditions hold: 

 
• Mutual Exclusivity: For any two distinct events Ai and Aj, where i ≠ j, their intersection is an empty set: Ai ∩ Aj = Φ. In other words, no outcomes are shared between any two different events. 
 
• Exhaustiveness: The union of all events, denoted as ⋃iAi, is equal to the entire sample space S. This means that every possible outcome in the sample space is covered by at least one of the events Ai.
 
• For an experiment with sample space S, the events Ai, i = 1, 2, 3, ..., are mutually exclusive if, for any distinct i and j (i ≠ j), the intersection of Ai and Aj is an empty set: Ai ∩ Aj = Φ.
 
• Additionally, the events Ai, i = 1, 2, 3, ..., are exhaustive if the union of all events is equal to the entire sample space: ⋃iAi = S.

**These conditions ensure that the events are distinct, with no overlapping outcomes, and that together they cover all possible outcomes in the sample space.**
